sentences: `s_load*`, `s_buffer_load*`, `buffer_load*` and `buffer_store*` use buffer device addresses (`PhysicalStorageBuffer64`).
LLVM `VCCTuple` scalar register lists ending in `vcc_lo,vcc_hi` (e.g.

`[s100,s101,s102,s103,s104,s105,vcc_lo,vcc_hi]`, `[s92,...,s105,vcc_lo,vcc_hi]`, seen in 6 FidelityFX FSPX shaders) are parsed as `slist` operands in `tools/shader_ir.py`, clear `vcc` from the lane-mask state in `tools/lane_masks.py`, and route `sN` slots to `%sgpr` and `vcc_lo`/`vcc_hi` to `%vcc`/`%vcc_hi` across SMEM loads, T#/S#/V# descriptor reads, and `global_*` `saddr`.
`src_scc` reads `%scc` (0 or 1, RDNA2 inline constant 253), matching `scc`.
`image_atomic_*` and `image_atomic_cmpswap` accept `a16` packed 16-bit unsigned coordinates (low half first, matching `image_store`).
CPU-checked by `tests/semantic/test_fspx_rules.py` and validated with `spirv-val` (native and `--wave64-emulate`).
**Not GPU-verified.** The base comes from the 64-bit SGPR pointer or the V# (dword0 \ | dword1[15:0] << 32), and the stride is V# dword1[29:16].
**The runtime must put the game's GPU heap in buffer-device-addressable memory at the same addresses the game writes into descriptors** (or remap them).
`s_load*` and `s_buffer_load*` take an immediate or an SGPR offset, or both at once (llvm-mc prints `sOFF offset:IMM`).

Rules, measured on AMD Radeon RX 6800 (gfx1030, Windows driver 32.0.21045.29003) by running the instructions as a raw compute kernel, wave32 and wave64 (155 runs, every result either 0 or the stored data, wave32 = wave64 in every dword): **address** = (base & ~3) + (sOFF & ~3) + (IMM & ~3) + 4·i for dword i: base, sOFF and IMM are each truncated to a multiple of 4, then added (`s_buffer_load_dword s9, s[24:27], 0x3` with base & 3 = 1 reads +0, not bytes 4..7; sOFF 3 + IMM 3 reads +0 and sOFF 2 + IMM 6 reads +4, where truncating the sum gives +4 and +8; sOFF 8 + IMM 4 reads +12; the same for `s_load*` with pointer & 3 = 1 or 3).

**`s_buffer_load*` bound**: dword i is 0, and memory is not read, when (sOFF & ~3) + (IMM & ~3) + 4·i + 4 > limit, with limit = NUM_RECORDS (V# dword2) bytes when the stride is 0 and NUM_RECORDS × stride bytes when it is not.

Per dword (x4 at 0xc with NUM_RECORDS 21: data, data, 0, 0; x8 at 0 with 21: five data, three 0), on the truncated offset (IMM 0x10 with NUM_RECORDS 18: 0; IMM 0x13 with 21: the dword at +0x10; sOFF 0xe + IMM 2 with 16: the dword at +0xc; sOFF 0x10 + IMM 4 with 20: 0), not seeing base & 3 (base & 3 = 3, IMM 0x13, NUM_RECORDS 20: data); with a stride the test is still on bytes (stride 4, NUM_RECORDS 5: IMM 0x10 data, 0x14 0; stride 1, NUM_RECORDS 17: IMM 0x10 is 0, so it is not an index test).
IMM is unsigned (0xffffc reads +0xffffc).
OOB_SELECT (V# word3[29:28]) 0, 1, 2 and 3 gave the same pattern (7 probes per value).

**`s_load*`**: no bound (+0x1ffffc reads the dword there); IMM is sign-extended from 21 bits and added in 64 bits (sOFF 8 + IMM −4 reads +4 where zero-extension reads 4 GiB further; sOFF 0xb + IMM −1 reads +4, so the negative IMM is truncated on its own: −1 → −4).

**Negative sums** (SHADER-336), measured on the integrated GPU of a Ryzen 9 9950X3D (gfx1036, RDNA2, Windows driver 32.0.21045.16010) with `tools/smem_neg_probe.py --oracle hw`, wave32 = wave64: `s_load` with IMM −4 or −0x40 and no sOFF, sOFF 4 + IMM −8, sOFF 0xc + IMM −0x20 and the x2 form with sOFF 4 + IMM −0x10 read below the pointer at the 64-bit signed sum, and sOFF 6 + IMM −1 reads +0 (4 + −4, each term truncated on its own).

`s_buffer_load` adds sOFF and IMM without wrapping at 32 bits: sOFF 0xfffffffc + IMM 8 and sOFF 0xfffffff0 + IMM 0x20 give 0 (past NUM_RECORDS 0x100), and sOFF 0xfffffffc, 0x80000000 and 0x7ffffffc alone give 0 (the translator has the same rule in both offset forms since #1686).

An `s_buffer_load` IMM with bit 20 set (llvm-mc rejects it; −4, −0x10, 0x100000 and 0x100004 were encoded by hand) reads data that is neither 0 nor the buffer's own words, differently in wave32 and wave64: the bound does not hold for that encoding, so no compiler output uses it and the translator does not model it.
`SmemHardwareRuleTests` in `tests/semantic/test_scalar_mem_smem.py` runs these rows with sOFF in a register and with sOFF known.
Not measured: `x16` (gets the x8 rule), NUM_RECORDS ≥ 2^31 and NUM_RECORDS × stride ≥ 2^32, V# dword1[31:30], and gfx1013 (PS5) itself.

`s_load`/`s_buffer_load` with sOFF + IMM < 0 (a negative IMM without sOFF included; the translator uses the 64-bit signed sum, an inference), an `s_buffer_load` IMM with bit 20 set (llvm-mc rejects it) or a negative one (kept as the 32-bit value: for stride 0 that is past any NUM_RECORDS below 4 GiB), `x16` (gets the x8 rule), sOFF ≥ 2^31, NUM_RECORDS ≥ 2^31 and NUM_RECORDS × stride ≥ 2^32, V# dword1[31:30], and gfx1013 (PS5) itself.

The translator checks each `s_buffer_load` dword with its own structured `if` and an `OpPhi` with 0, so an out-of-range dword issues no load (when descriptor limit and offset are compile-time constants, in-range dwords fold to straight-line loads and out-of-range dwords emit constant zero without branches); `s_load` stays straight-line.
Before this the translator added base + sOFF + IMM unaligned, had no `s_buffer_load` bound and zero-extended a negative `s_load` IMM.

Checked by `tests/semantic/test_scalar_mem_smem.py` (`SmemHardwareRuleTests`, the measurement's rows, values and the addresses read; `SmemSoffsetImmTranslatorTests`) and by the GPU tests `runtime/test/shaders/cs_smem_soffset_imm.asm`, `cs_smem_bounds.asm`, `cs_smem_stride_align.asm` and `cs_smem_sload_neg.asm` (never run that one with a translator that zero-extends the immediate: it reads 4 GiB past the heap), all in `check.py` and `scripts/run_gpu_tests.py`, which pass on the RX 6800 (Vulkan, driver 26.11.2).
See *Buffer bounds checking* below for the MUBUF `num_records` checks.

**A constant SGPR offset** (`s_mov_b32 s12, C`, folded at translate time) is added as the run-time path adds `sOFF`: zero-extended, `& ~3`, after the immediate has been normalised (unsigned for `s_buffer_load`, 21-bit signed for `s_load`), with no 32-bit wrap.

Until 2026-11-22 (#1686) the fold added it before the truncation, so `s12 = -4` with `offset:20` read byte 16 instead of being out of range, and an `s_load` `sOFF` of 2^20 or more was sign-extended from 21 bits (found by @Impre-visible; hardware measured by @Pierre-Kookis on gfx1036: 0xFFFFFFFC + 20 reads 0).
CPU-checked by `tests/semantic/test_smem_const_offset.py` (each case constant vs run-time offset, and against the measured rule).
